body:
### Summary

Currently, `UV_PYTHON` seems to have basically two distinguishable meanings:

1. Prefer this interpreter when creating a virtual environment
2. Use this interpreter's default environment for `uv pip` operations

. I, as a NixOS user with a OS-managed Python, would love to use `UV_PYTHON` for the first, but never the second.

Now I need to take care to set `UV_PYTHON` only for operations that create virtual environments and unset it for other operations.

I think a useful and backwards compatible model could be something like:

- Have `UV_PYTHON` behave exactly as it does currently
- Introduce a new environment variable `UV_BASE_PYTHON`, with the semantics of only affecting interpreter choice when creating a new venv, but not other uv operations.

### Example

Consider this behavior:

```
$ echo $UV_PYTHON
/nix/store/gxzhl7aaiid7zp3y47jqqiq7zg5mqpwp-python3-3.14.6/bin/python

$ uv venv new-venv
Using CPython 3.14.6 interpreter at: /nix/store/gxzhl7aaiid7zp3y47jqqiq7zg5mqpwp-python3-3.14.6/bin/python
Creating virtual environment at: new-venv
Activate with: source new-venv/bin/activate

$ source new-venv/bin/activate

(new-venv)
$ uv pip install setuptools
Using Python 3.14.6 environment at: /nix/store/gxzhl7aaiid7zp3y47jqqiq7zg5mqpwp-python3-3.14.6
error: The interpreter at /nix/store/gxzhl7aaiid7zp3y47jqqiq7zg5mqpwp-python3-3.14.6 is externally managed, and indicates the following:

  This command has been disabled as it tries to modify the immutable
  `/nix/store` filesystem.

  To use Python with Nix and nixpkgs, have a look at the online documentation:
  <https://nixos.org/manual/nixpkgs/stable/

hint: Consider creating a virtual environment, e.g., with `uv venv`

$
```

The `uv venv` command did what I wanted. However, `uv pip install` did not (IIUC https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/6612 is a discussion related to this, but, also IIUC, not quite the same thing).

Instead, with my proposed `UV_BASE_PYTHON` this could look like this: 

```
$ echo $UV_PYTHON

$ echo $UV_BASE_PYTHON
/nix/store/gxzhl7aaiid7zp3y47jqqiq7zg5mqpwp-python3-3.14.6/bin/python

$ uv venv new-venv
Using CPython 3.14.6 interpreter at: /nix/store/gxzhl7aaiid7zp3y47jqqiq7zg5mqpwp-python3-3.14.6/bin/python
Creating virtual environment at: new-venv
Activate with: source new-venv/bin/activate

$ source new-venv/bin/activate

(new-venv)
$ uv pip install setuptools
... successfully uses the venv
$
```
title: Provide a way to select the interpreter used for venv creation without overriding installation target of `uv pip`
